full_judgment:
Md Aminul Islam, J: On an application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed by the petitioners, a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why inclusion of the case land measuring 3400 acres out of 6400 acres situated within Upzilla-Mymensingh Sadar, Mouza-Akua, JL No.79, Serial No.2, SA Khatian No.236 and 237, Plot No.1323 published in the Bangladesh Gazette Additional issue dated 10-12-2012 (Annexure-G) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders to be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The petitioners case in short is that the SA recorded tenant Modan Mohan died leaving a son Haripada Dey, who inherited 171/2 decimal of land from plot No.1323. Thereafter, Haripada sold out 6½+ 5½ in total 12 decimals of land from plot No.1323 to the petitioner No.1 by two registered deeds, namely Deed No.11772 dated 26-6-1978 and Deed No.20381 dated 14-12-1979 and delivered possession accordingly. The said Haripada also transferred 5 decimal of land to the petitioner No.2 by a registered Deed No.20357 dated 14-12-1979 and delivered possession to her. In such way, the petitioners got (17+12+5) 34 decimals of land in plot No.1323. Thereafter, it was detected that the Khatian number was wrongly mentioned in aforesaid three deeds being Nos.11772, 20357 and 20381 wherein old Khatian No.272 new Khatian No.237 was written instead of old Khatian No.271 new Khatian No.236. Haripada Dey executed three correction deeds vide Deed Nos. 9534, 9536 and 9540 dated 2-5-1981. The petitioners mutated their name in the office of the respondent No.4 in respect-of their purchased land from Haripada Dey to the extent of 17 decimals of land vide Mutation Case No.1041 (IX-1) 87-88, obtained DCR and paid rent upto 1422 BS. The petitioner No.1 mutated his name in the office of the respondent No.4 vide Mutation Case No.293 (My/80-81) in respect of 1.15 acres of land which he acquired by way of inheritance from his father including the land in question from plot No.1323 to the extent of 17 decimals and paid rent to the office of the respondents upto 1422 BS 

 7. Mr Swapan Kumar Mitra, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the SA recorded tenant Dinanath Dey of SA Khatian No.237 and Madan Mohan Dey of SA Khatian No.236 died on 18-5-1975 and 14-12-1971 respectively at their village Akua chukaitala Hindupara, Mymensingh Sadar Upazila, Mymensingh. They never left this country for India at the time of indo-Pak War in 1965 and, as such, the enlistment of the property in question as vested property in "Ka" list is without jurisdiction. He further submits that the Government never took possession of the case property as enemy or vested property and, as such, the enlistment of the case land as vested property in the "Ka" list is absolutely illegal. He further submits that after the death of SA recorded tenant Dinanath Dey, father of Dijendra Chandra Dey, mutated his name in respect of 17 decimal of land in Plot No.1323 of SA Khatian No.237 along with other land vide Mutation Case No. 293(my/80-81). He submits that the petitioners are husband and wife, they purchased 17 decimals of land from SA Khatian No.236 Plot No.1323 from Haripada Dey son of late Modan Mohan Dey by three registered deed being Nos. 11772, 20381, 20357 dated 26-6-1978 and 14-12-1979 and mutated their names in the office of the respondent No.4 vide mutation case No.1041(IX-1)/87-88, then obtained DCR and the Tahsilder of the concerned Tahsil office accepted rent of the suit land and granted rent receipt upon 1422 BS He further submits that since the law of vested property was repealed (Ordinance No.1 of 1969) on 23-3-1974, no further vested property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead. Accordingly, there is no basis to treat the case land as vested property. 

 8. Mr AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, the learned Assistant Attorney-General (AAG) appearing on behalf of the respondents submits that Modan Mohan Dey, Romoni Mohan Dey, Mohani Mohan Dey Pabitra Mohan Dey were the real owner of the schedule "Ka" land of Mouza-Akua, Mymensingh, but they left the country and went to India in 1965 and, as such, VP Case No.11(Ka)/94-95 dated 3-7-1970 was initiated against SA Khatian No.236, 237 and SA plot No.1323, hearing an area (0.52+0.17)= 0.69 acres of land. But this petitioner created an unregistered Power of Attorney through forgery, which he filed before the Tribunal claiming the scheduled land. He further submits that the petitioners have no locus standi to file the writ petition and the writ petition is not maintainable. He lastly submits that matters relating to Vested Property application are to be filed to the Arpita Tribunal and the High Court Division cannot determine the title of land without taking evidence. We have carefully perused the writ petition, annexures and other materials on record.
